result.rationale: MultiEmail.tsx renders value.map((field, index) => <li key={index}> with controlled EmailField inputs, and the remove handler does updatedValue.splice(index, 1). With index-based keys, React reuses components when a middle item is removed, so subsequent inputs can show stale text from the removed row's state; the mechanism is fully visible in the new file and this is a real correctness defect in the newly added component.

judged_text: MultiEmail list keyed by index with splice removal causes stale/uncontrolled input state when removing middle rows

record.issue_text: MultiEmail list keyed by index with splice removal causes stale/uncontrolled input state when removing middle rows

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the list renders inputs with `key={index}` and removes an entry via `updatedValue.splice(index, 1)`. Using array indices as keys in a mutable list can cause React to reuse component instances for different rows after a middle deletion, which can lead to mismatched UI state (e.g., focus/cursor jumping or any internal state inside `EmailField` being associated with the wrong email) even though `value` is passed as a prop.
